html:
The settlement of Turkic peoples in Anatolia after the Battle of Manzikert in 1071, which turned a Greek speaking Christian land slowly into a Turkish and Muslim one.

With the Byzantines locked in civil war, Turkmen tribes with their herds spread across the central plateau, whose grasslands suited them. A Seljuk prince, Suleiman ibn Qutalmish, took Nicaea, near Constantinople, and around 1077 founded the Sultanate of Rum, "Rum" meaning the land of the Romans. After the crusaders took Nicaea in 1097 the sultans moved their capital to Konya. Other Turkish dynasties, such as the Danishmendids, ruled in the northeast.

The change took centuries. Greek and Armenian Christians lived on in many towns, and many people converted or married in. Persian became the language of the court and of poets such as Rumi in Konya. Europeans were calling the region "Turchia" by the late 12th century. After the Mongols broke Seljuk power, small Turkish states arose, one of which became the Ottoman Empire.
sum: The settlement of Turkic peoples in Anatolia after the Battle of Manzikert in 1071, which turned a Greek speaking Christian land slowly into a Turkish and Muslim one.
